quiz.problem: Goal 3 promises the reader can explain task graph, frontier, worktrees, one integration branch and one review at the end. The Final test only covers the integration branch (predict-run-end) and the review at the end (spot-midrun-review). Nothing tests the frontier or the task graph; only the shared-file Checkpoint touches them, and Checkpoints don't count. scenario-whole-spec is also recognition, not transfer. Its prompt repeats every prerequisite from the body and the docs table word for word ('split into six tickets with blocking edges', 'runs sub-agents in the background, each in its own worktree', 'one run to land them all'), so `/implement-spec` is the only option that matches. Two distractors are straw men: `/tdd` once per ticket, and `/code-review` with nothing built.
quiz.evidence: Body line 132: 'The frontier is every ticket whose blockers have all landed, and every frontier ticket runs at once.' docs/engineering/implement-spec.md:5 and :21 ('Without edges the graph is flat and every ticket starts at once'). Writing guide: 'Every goal gets at least one Final test question' and 'Questions test transfer, not recognition... Don't restate the defining phrase of the right answer in the prompt.' The research note's candidate Q2 is nearly the same question.
quiz.fix:
Replace scenario-whole-spec with a frontier prediction (scenario- count drops to 4, still at least 3; ids aren't published yet):

```test predict-frontier
An `/implement-spec` run has five tickets. A has no blockers. B and C are each blocked by A. D is blocked by B. E is blocked by C and D. Ticket A has just merged into the integration branch. What starts now?
- [ ] B only, because tickets are built in the order they're numbered.
  > The tickets form a graph, not a list. Order on the tracker doesn't set the pace; blockers do.
- [x] B and C, each in its own worktree.
  > Right. Both had only A as a blocker, so both join the frontier, and every frontier ticket runs at once.
- [ ] B, C, D and E, because A was the only ticket with no blockers.
  > D still waits for B, and E waits for C and D. Only tickets whose blockers have all landed are on the frontier.
- [ ] Nothing until code-review has checked ticket A.
  > The run's one review comes after every ticket has landed, not between merges.
```

If you keep a Skill-choice question for goal 2 instead, make it need judgement. For example: "Your events-page spec has six tickets, and after 01 lands, 02, 03 and 04 can all start. Your harness runs background sub-agents in worktrees, and you'd rather review one finished branch than six commits. In a cleared session, what do you type?" Options: `/implement` with all six ticket numbers / `/implement-spec` with the spec's path [x] / `/implement` on 02, 03 and 04 in three terminals opened in the same project folder (feedback: sessions sharing one checkout amend each other's commits) / `/tdd` once per ticket.

quiz.problem: Three questions test the same rule: `/clear` between tickets. The Checkpoint's right answer (`/clear`, then `/implement` for ticket 02) is the same lesson as spot-no-clear's right answer ('She never typed `/clear` between tickets'). It also overlaps serial-harness's right answer ('once per ticket, clearing between them'). The Checkpoint's 'two tickets together' distractor matches spot-no-clear's 'all at once'. That breaks 'no Checkpoint duplicates a Final test question'. Meanwhile a rule from the same section goes untested: never run two `/implement` sessions in one checkout.
quiz.evidence: Writing guide: 'no Checkpoint duplicates a Final test question.' Body line 84: 'don't run two `/implement` sessions in one checkout: one user's sessions amended each other's commits, because they shared one folder.' No question tests this.
quiz.fix:
Rewrite the Checkpoint (it sits right after this section, so placement stays correct). It needs a new id, because the meaning changes:

```checkpoint two-terminals
Your book-club spec has tickets 02 and 03, and neither blocks the other. To save time, you open a second terminal in the same project folder and start `/implement` on 03 while 02 is still building in the first. What's likely to go wrong?
- [ ] Nothing. Each session has its own context window, so they can't affect each other.
  > Separate windows don't mean separate files. Both sessions edit and commit in the same folder.
- [x] The two sessions edit the same checkout, so their changes and commits get tangled.
  > Right. One checkout means one working folder. To build in parallel, use `/implement-spec`, which gives each ticket its own worktree.
- [ ] The second `/implement` refuses to start until the first one commits.
  > It doesn't check for other sessions. That's why the clash happens silently.
- [ ] Ticket 03 skips tdd, because only one session can load a Skill at a time.
  > Each session loads its own Skills. The problem is the shared folder, not the Skills.
```
